name: Reykjavík Eco Campsite (Laugardalur)
summary: Located in lush Laugardalur park directly beside Laugardalslaug—Reykjavík’s largest geothermal swimming pool with seven hot tubs and a steam bath. Ideal first or final night base 45 minutes from KEF Airport.

name: Þingvellir National Park Campsite (Leirar)
summary: Camp inside a UNESCO World Heritage site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates drift apart. Quiet birch-wooded pitches within walking distance of Almannagjá gorge and Silfra fissure.

name: Úlfljótsvatn Lakeside Campsite
summary: One of the best family and campervan campsites on the Golden Circle, set on the shores of Lake Úlfljótsvatn just south of Þingvellir. Accepts the Iceland Camping Card and has spacious level grass zones.

name: Reykjamörk Hveragerði Geothermal Campsite
summary: Sheltered by mature trees in the geothermal town of Hveragerði—just 5 minutes from the trailhead for the Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River hike.

name: Skógar Campsite (Beneath Skógafoss Waterfall)
summary: Pitch your tent or park your campervan on flat grass directly facing the 60-meter curtain of Skógafoss. Unbeatable for photographing the waterfall under the Midnight Sun or Northern Lights after day-trippers leave.

name: Vík í Mýrdal Campsite
summary: Located 5 minutes from Reynisfjara black sand beach and Dyrhólaey puffin cliffs. Features a large heated indoor dining hall and kitchen—a lifesaver during windy South Coast evenings.

name: Þakgil Canyon Campsite (Natural Cave Dining Hall)
location: South Iceland (22 km inland from Vík via Route 214)
summary: Arguably Iceland’s most atmospheric campsite: a dramatic moss-walled canyon that blocks coastal gales, featuring a communal candlelit dining hall with grills inside a natural volcanic rock cave.

name: Kirkjubæjarklaustur Campsite (Kirkjubær II)
summary: Sheltered beneath steep green cliffs 10 minutes east of Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon. Well-Protected from wind with grassy pitches and easy walking access to Systrafoss waterfall and the town swimming pool.

name: Skaftafell Campground (Vatnajökull National Park)
summary: Basecamp beneath Europe’s largest ice cap. Step straight out of your tent or campervan onto the trail to basalt-columned Svartifoss waterfall and guided glacier hikes on Falljökull, 45 minutes from Jökulsárlón.

name: Höfn Camping Ground (Vestrahorn & Glacier Views)
summary: Panoramic views across the Hornafjörður lagoon toward three Vatnajökull outlet glaciers, 15 minutes from dramatic Vestrahorn (Stokksnes) black sand dunes and walking distance to Höfn’s famous langoustine restaurants.

name: Egilsstaðir Camp & Hostel (East Iceland Hub)
summary: One of the highest-rated year-round facilities on the Ring Road: 24/7 heated bathrooms, outdoor dishwashing stations, luggage lockers, and easy day-trip access to Vök Baths, Seyðisfjörður, and Stuðlagil Canyon.

name: Borgarfjörður Eystri Campsite (Hafnarhólmi Puffins)
location: Eastfjords (70 km from Egilsstaðir via Route 94)
summary: Built directly around Álfaborg ("Elf Rock") in a tranquil fjord village 5 minutes from Hafnarhólmi marina, where 10,000+ Atlantic puffins nest within arm’s reach between May and mid-August.

name: Mývatn Lakeside Campsite (Hlíð / Reykjahlíð)
summary: Set amidst lava fields overlooking Lake Mývatn, 5 minutes from Mývatn Nature Baths, Hverir boiling mud pots, and Krafla volcanic crater. Tip: Pack a head net in June/July for harmless lakeside midges.

name: Ásbyrgi Canyon Campground (Vatnajökull NP North)
summary: Tucked inside a giant horseshoe-shaped canyon with 100-meter vertical cliffs and a dense birch forest. One of the warmest, most wind-sheltered microclimates anywhere in Iceland.

name: Húsavík Campground (Whale Capital & Geosea)
summary: Conveniently located at the northern entrance to Húsavík—5 minutes from the whale watching harbor and the clifftop Geosea Geothermal Sea Baths overlooking Skjálfandi Bay.

name: Hamrar Outdoor Recreation Area (Akureyri)
location: North Iceland (Kjarnaskógur Forest • 4 km from Akureyri)
summary: Sprawling across tree-lined zones bordering Kjarnaskógur forest. Features heated service buildings, laundry, boat rentals, and easy access to downtown Akureyri and the Forest Lagoon.

name: Stykkishólmur Campsite (Snæfellsnes & Ferry Port)
summary: Steps from Stykkishólmur’s mineral thermal pool, Súgandisey lighthouse, and the Baldur ferry terminal to the Westfjords. Only 25 minutes from iconic Mt. Kirkjufell.

name: Arnarstapi & Olafsvík Coastal Campsites
summary: Sleep right between the glacier-capped cone of Snæfellsjökull volcano and the basalt sea arches of Arnarstapi and Hellnar. Ideal base for Djúpalónssandur beach and whale watching from Ólafsvík.

name: Tungudalur Waterfall Campsite (Ísafjörður, Westfjords)
summary: Nestled in a birch-forested valley with the Buná river and waterfall cascading right through the campground. Perfect basecamp for exploring Dynjandi waterfall and Hornstrandir nature reserve boats.

name: Landmannalaugar Highland Basecamp (F208)
summary: Set beside a natural geothermal bathing river surrounded by rainbow rhyolite mountains and obsidian lava fields. Tip: Park your 4x4 at the footbridge lot BEFORE the deep river crossing.
